name: Round 11: the Syndicate broadcast airship, round 2 (the lead's 'still just a blimp')
why: The lead rejected all three of round 1, on airship_r11_a (the Zeppelin liner, his best of three): 'Of the 3, this is the best one, but it also still just kind of looks like a blimp instead of slightly satirical dystopian broadcasting airship of the syndicate'. The diagnosis: round 1 optimised RIGID and produced three gas envelopes with a screen attached. The operative word was BROADCASTING. At his pose the airship is ~880 px wide and read almost entirely as SILHOUETTE, and an ellipsoid silhouette is a blimp whatever is pressed into the skin -- so the broadcast apparatus has to BREAK the silhouette, not decorate the hull. Every direction below hangs the screen OFF the hull at a scale that dominates it, and carries the surveillance-and-PA hardware that makes the satire structural: horn speaker clusters, gimballed camera blisters, a searchlight, antenna masts. Satire per the lead's standing rule (announcer humour): believable, never a punchline -- the joke is institutional over-seriousness, a vast immaculate municipal machine whose whole purpose is to sell at you and film you while it does it. The screen aperture is an EMPTY framed opening: AdBroadcast's quad fills it in engine (ad_screen.gd:34), so the model must provide the frame, never a picture.
tail: Full aircraft in frame, three-quarter front view from slightly above, isolated on a plain dark grey studio background, no ground, no people, no text, no logos. Photorealistic, gritty, high detail, cinematic lighting, grounded real-world materials.

syndicate.label: Syndicate airship
syndicate.intro: Round 2. Your note on the Zeppelin: still a blimp, not a satirical dystopian broadcasting airship. So the screen is no longer a window in the hull -- it is bigger than the hull and hung off it, and each ship carries the loudspeakers and cameras that say what it is really for. The screen openings are EMPTY frames; the live feed of your kills renders into them in engine. Approve ONE, or tell me which half of which one to keep.
syndicate.lead: Photorealistic concept art of a {role} roughly 26 metres long, a corporate advertising and surveillance platform that drifts low over a neon city at night broadcasting at the people below.
syndicate.look: Immaculate ivory and cold off-white enamel panels with almost no rust, fine panel seams and flush rivets, brushed gunmetal structural steel, and the apparatus of an institution that is addressing you: clusters of grey horn loudspeakers, gimballed black camera blisters on short stalks, a swivelling searchlight, whip antennas and a small dish, stencilled maintenance hatches and inspection plates. Steady navigation lights only, red port and green starboard, and a cold white glow from the gondola windows. Clinical, expensive, faintly bureaucratic and slightly sinister: municipal infrastructure that sells things. Over-engineered for the job it does, and completely serious about it.

role_notes.airship: Read as SILHOUETTE at ~880 px from the RTS camera, drifting down the avenue at 12 m between 24 m blocks. The outline must not be an ellipse: the screen structure has to stand outside the hull's profile so the shape says 'broadcast rig', not 'balloon'. Each screen opening must be a FLAT, EMPTY, vertical rectangular frame -- the engine fills it.

concepts.title: Gantry rig: a billboard that happens to fly
concepts.subject: A slender rigid airship hull clamped inside a heavy external steel gantry that runs its whole length, like scaffolding around a tower. Hung from each side of the gantry is one enormous EMPTY rectangular screen frame, taller and longer than the hull itself, so the square billboard outline dominates the rounded hull hiding behind it. Bundles of cable and conduit run along the gantry, horn loudspeaker clusters are bolted at each corner, and a boxy control gondola with a glazed front hangs beneath the midpoint.
concepts.notes: Takes what you liked about the Zeppelin and buries it inside the rig. The silhouette is a rectangle with a ship inside it, which is the single biggest change from round 1. This is my pick.

concepts.title: Twin hull: the thing with the screen in its mouth
concepts.subject: A catamaran airship: two slender parallel rigid hulls held apart by braced cross-spars, with one colossal EMPTY rectangular screen frame filling the entire gap between them like a sail stretched in a frame. A long armoured gondola bristling with gimballed camera blisters and horn loudspeakers is slung beneath the centre spar, ducted engine pods sit at the tail of each hull, and a searchlight is mounted on the forward cross-spar.
concepts.notes: The most unmistakable silhouette in the game and impossible to read as a blimp. RISK: two hulls is an odd, expensive-looking machine; it may read more alien than corporate.

concepts.title: Broadcast barge: the flying municipal tower
concepts.subject: An angular flat-bottomed aerial barge with a hard chined hull and a stepped superstructure, built like a harbour vessel rather than an aircraft. Its flanks are one long EMPTY rectangular screen frame running most of the length in a heavy steel surround, and its open upper deck is crowded with apparatus: a stacked cluster of grey horn loudspeakers facing outward in every direction, three gimballed camera blisters on stalks, a satellite dish, a lattice antenna mast and a swivelling searchlight, all behind a low railing and a catwalk.
concepts.notes: The most obviously 'institution addressing you' of the three, and the cluttered deck reads well from above, which is the angle you actually have. RISK: flat-bottomed and deck-heavy, it may read as a boat or a barge rather than something flying.
